rationale:
Evidence: 119 of 120 development trials across iterations 1 to 5 ended off_track. The one finish was an oval run in iteration 4 (score 939 on that seed). The best design so far is iteration 5 (99.67), with max_error 0.060 to 0.063 against a fixed off-track limit of 0.06 m. The limit cannot be raised: for body_width 0.12 it is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03), and body_width/4 stays below 0.06 across the allowed range. Score is driven by progress, since no run completed, so keeping the robot on the tape longer is the main lever.

Key observation: iteration 6 changed kp (1.5 to 2.5) and base_speed (1.4 to 1.2), yet every per-track metric matched iteration 5 to four decimals. Gain and speed changes therefore do not reach the failure point. I conclude the failure is set by the plant's response, not by the steering gain. The robot's yaw response is likely too slow or too sluggish relative to the sensor lead, so it drifts out before the controller acts.

Changes, chosen to alter the plant's response, which the last two iterations did not do:
(1) Reduce yaw inertia. Yaw inertia is mass*(L^2+W^2)/12. Mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg and body_length 0.18 to 0.12 m cut it by about 45 percent, so the robot turns faster for the same wheel differential.
(2) Narrow wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m. Turn rate is the wheel-speed difference divided by track, so the same PWM gives about 20 percent more yaw rate.
(3) Move the sensors slightly forward to y = 0.06 m for more lead. The spacing (0.008 m) and 8 mm footprint from iteration 5 are kept, since that sensing is the best so far.
(4) kp 2.0 (from 1.5) for steering authority, kd 0.6 and ki 0.1 unchanged, and base_speed 1.3 (from 1.4) to leave time to correct at bends. Speed is kept near the 1.5 m/s needed to finish.

Expected result: lower max_error (target under 0.06), fewer line-loss events, and progress above 0.4 on the oval and s-bend. Because I changed several things at once, the next telemetry may not isolate the cause, so I will treat the result as evidence for the plant-response hypothesis rather than a clean test. The slalom remains the hardest track.
